web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: What the Market Is Pricing In at $318.71
question: What future free cash flow growth and terminal multiple are embedded in TSM's $1,561.80B enterprise value after a 20.1% weekly selloff, and why does the market discount a 13.81x forward P/E?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. In capital-intensive monopolies, the spread between the two is governed by the capex cycle.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Principle

web_blocks.title: Deconstructing the $318.71 Price Tag & Rapid Multiple Compression

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $318.71 ($319.14 on TradingView), TSMC carries a $1,652.98 billion market cap on Finviz ($1,570.36B on TradingView) [28, 29, 35]. Its enterprise value dropped to $1,561.80 billion, shedding roughly $415 billion in one week [29]. On trailing results ($156.42B sales, $80.58B net income), TSM trades at 20.51x trailing P/E and 13.70x EV/EBITDA [29]. It trades at 9.98x EV/Sales, 7.52x price-to-book, and 33.14x price-to-free-cash-flow [29]. Forward consensus places TSM at 13.81x forward P/E and a 0.34 PEG ratio against a $554.22 Street target [29].

Paying 13.81x forward earnings for 64.77% gross margins, 57.78% operating margins, 32.67% ROIC, and 41.98% ROE looks unusually cheap [29]. Q3 2026 revenue grew 41.2% YoY, and October sales jumped 59.7% YoY to NT$586.89 billion [5, 22]. Yet the market discounts $318.71 for five concrete reasons. First, FY2026 capex is surging to $60B–$64B, backed by $40.93B in November 10 Board approvals [4, 23]. Second, overseas fabs in Arizona, Kumamoto, and Dresden bring 2%–4% gross margin dilution [10, 13]. Third, the November 10 Board approved up to $1.5B in AI ecosystem equity stakes, while Q3 footnotes revealed NT$359.48B in refundable customer deposits and a NT$63.20B non-cash VIS gain [21, 23]. Fourth, Section 232 25% tariff proclamations and Nanjing export-license rules add policy friction [1]. Fifth, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield sits at 5.04% inside a broad US market Downtrend [34].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: What $1,561.80B Enterprise Value Demands

web_blocks.html: To strip away market panic, we invert the valuation model. We apply a 9.5% WACC—anchored by the 5.04% US 10-year Treasury yield [34], equity risk, and a 100 bps Taiwan premium—plus 3.5% terminal growth (16.7x terminal FCF). Finviz's 33.14x P/FCF on a $1,652.98B market cap implies $49.88B in TTM free cash flow [29]. Solving backward, $1,561.80B EV requires $49.88B TTM FCF to compound at just 11.3% annually over ten years.

web_blocks.the_number: 11.3% 10-Year Implied FCF CAGR (on $49.88B TTM FCF; 17.2% on FY25 $31.96B trough)
web_blocks.how_calculated: Solved for the 10-year FCF compounding rate that equates discounted FCF (Years 1–10) plus terminal value (Year 10 FCF x (1 + g) / (WACC - g)) to EV of $1,561.80B.
web_blocks.the_inputs: EV = $1,561.80B; Finviz TTM FCF = $49.88B; Audited FY25 FCF = $31.96B ($72.52B CFO - $40.56B CapEx); 9M 2026 FCF = NT$1,112.15B (~$34.9B, including +NT$169.62B customer deposit inflows after ~$40.5B 9M CapEx); Implied Q4 2026 CapEx = $19.5B–$23.5B within $60B–$64B FY26 guide; WACC = 9.5%; Terminal g = 3.5%.
web_blocks.the_range: 8.5%–9.5% CAGR on $60B+ normalized owner earnings once capex intensity eases after 2027; 14%–17% CAGR if measured from deposit-adjusted 9M26 annualized FCF (~$39.4B ex-deposit surge) or FY2025's $31.96B trough.
web_blocks.if_off: If AI hyperscaler capex pauses in 2027–2028 and drops fab utilization below 75% while depreciation from $60B+ annual capex hits COGS and tool commitments keep spending elevated, FCF compresses to ~$25B–$35B (or ~$35B–$42B only if management slashes ~$40B+ growth capex back toward ~$20B maintenance), pushing fair EV toward $1,100B–$1,300B (~$215–$250/share).

web_blocks.html: Reconciling cash flow periods clarifies why Finviz's $49.88B TTM FCF sits above audited FY2025 FCF ($31.96B) [1, 29]. In 9M 2026, TSMC generated NT$1,112.15B (~$34.9B) of FCF after spending NT$1,289.97B (~$40.5B) on PP&E [21]. That 9M cash flow included +NT$169.62B (~$5.3B) in net customer deposit inflows as temporary receipts rose from NT$189.86B to NT$359.48B [21]. Meanwhile, ~$40.5B of 9M capex leaves $19.5B–$23.5B of implied Q4 2026 capex inside the $60B–$64B annual budget [4, 21]. Adjusting for Q4 capex and customer deposits puts normalized FY2026 FCF closer to $35B–$42B, while a sub-75% utilization downturn could compress FCF to ~$25B–$35B.

web_blocks.title: Peer Comparison: Merchant Monopoly vs. Foundry, Packaging & AI Peers

web_blocks.html: Comparing TSMC against foundry, OSAT packaging, and AI peers highlights its profitability gap alongside broad Stage 4 selling [33].

web_blocks.caption: TSM vs. Foundry, OSAT Packaging, AI Silicon & Mega-Cap Peers (Snapshot 2026-11-20)
web_blocks.takeaway: TSM pairs 41.98% ROE and 57.78% operating margin at 20.54x trailing P/E, crushing trailing foundry peers UMC (19.83% ROE, 11.45x P/E) and INTC (-10.87% ROE). Nearly every semiconductor peer—including NVDA, TXN, UMC, ASX, and INTC—also sits in Stage 4 distribution.

web_blocks.html: The live peer snapshot confirms that TSMC has no true public-market substitute, yet semiconductor stocks are selling off together [33]. United Microelectronics (UMC, $12.04, $30.49B cap) trades at 11.45x trailing and 10.73x forward P/E with 19.83% ROE, stuck in mature nodes [33]. Intel (INTC, $51.28, $272.55B cap) posts -10.87% ROE and 10.51% operating margin while trading at 28.53x forward earnings [17, 33]. ASE Technology (ASX, $26.27, $61.09B cap), TSMC's key OSAT packaging partner, trades at 24.90x trailing P/E with just 11.46% operating margin [33]. Even top client NVIDIA (NVDA, $125.53, 13.49x P/E, 93.33% YoY sales growth) and analog giant Texas Instruments (TXN, $263.75, 34.22x P/E) sit in Stage 4 [33]. Only Microsoft (MSFT, $484.52, 25.30x P/E, 34.22% ROE) holds Stage 3 above its major base [33].

web_blocks.region_era: Korea / U.S. Semiconductor Memory & Capex Cycles (2018–2023)
web_blocks.mechanism: In the 2017–2018 and 2021–2022 upcycles, memory leaders posted 50%+ gross margins and looked cheap at 6x–10x trailing P/E. Then hyperscaler inventory digestion and heavy capex collided with rising depreciation.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: In 2022–2023, Micron's sales dropped 49% YoY ($30.8B to $15.5B) and gross margin swung from +45% to -9%. Samsung's Device Solutions unit posted multi-billion-dollar losses despite looking cheap on peak multiples.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: TSMC's foundry model has far stronger lock-in and pricing power than commodity memory. Still, the trap is identical: a 13.81x forward P/E does not stop a Stage 4 liquidation when $60B+ capex commitments meet rate and tariff fears.

web_blocks.title: Capex Intensity vs. Owner Earnings & Balance Sheet Buffer

web_blocks.html: At $318.71, TSMC's balance sheet provides immense long-term downside protection even as the tape bleeds [21, 29]. As of September 30, 2026, cash and current marketable securities reached NT$4,016.72 billion (~$126.0B) against NT$1,031.58 billion (~$32.36B) in total debt [21]. That puts net cash at $93.64 billion—roughly 5.7% of TSM's $1,652.98B market cap [21, 29]. Maintenance capex on 17M+ wafers runs ~$18B–$22B per year, so over $40B of FY2026 capex is discretionary N2, A16, and CoWoS expansion [4, 9]. Still, the $40.93B November 10 capex authorization locks in higher depreciation through 2028 [23].

web_blocks.title: Why Cheap Multiples Fail in a Stage 4 Downtrend
paragraphs: TSM's 13.81x forward P/E and 0.34 PEG look compelling on a spreadsheet [29]. Yet history from 2022 proves that institutional de-grossing ignores forward multiples until selling exhausts itself [30]. At a 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield and 10 market distribution days, funds sell liquid winners first [34, 35]. Waiting for the tape to base protects capital far better than guessing a multiple bottom.

web_blocks.html: Valuation at $318.71 creates a sharp split between long-term intrinsic value and near-term tape risk [29]. TSMC's 32.67% ROIC against a 9.5% WACC yields a +23.2 percentage point economic spread [29]. Yet cheap valuation is not a timing trigger when the stock drops 9.48% in one session on 2.38x volume [35]. Fundamental value sets our $425.00 Base and $550.00 Bull targets for the next cycle, while Stage 4 technicals enforce discipline today [28].

book_paragraphs: With TSMC's business quality and footnote nuances established, we confront the market's verdict on November 20, 2026. At $318.71 per ADR, TSMC carries a $1,652.98 billion market cap and a $1,561.80 billion enterprise value. In a single week, the stock fell 20.07%, erasing more than $400 billion in market value.

That drop compressed TSMC's valuation multiples dramatically. Trailing P/E fell from 25.66x to 20.51x, EV/EBITDA fell from 17.34x to 13.70x, and forward P/E sank to 13.81x with a 0.34 PEG ratio against a $554.22 consensus target. For a company growing Q3 revenue 41.2% YoY and October sales 59.7% YoY with 64.77% gross margins and 32.67% ROIC, 13.81x forward earnings looks absurdly cheap.

Yet markets rarely slash a $2 trillion leader by 20% in five days without real anxieties. Five overhangs explain the discount: $60B to $64B in FY2026 capex plus $40.93B in November 10 Board capex approvals; 2% to 4% overseas fab gross margin dilution; $1.5B in new Anthropic and OpenAI equity commitments; Section 232 25% chip tariff risks; and a 5.04% U.S. 10-year Treasury yield inside a broad equity Downtrend.

Our job is to separate fundamental worth from near-term market plumbing. Cheap multiples tell us what TSMC can earn once sellers finish liquidating, not whether tomorrow's close will be higher than today's.

book_callouts.title: The Reverse DCF at $1,561.80 Billion EV
book_callouts.text: At a 9.5% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth, $1,561.80B EV requires $49.88B TTM FCF to compound at 11.3% annually over ten years. Because Q4 capex ($19.5B–$23.5B implied) and +NT$169.62B deposit inflows skew trailing FCF, a sub-75% utilization downturn could compress FCF toward $25B–$35B.

book_subsections.title: Walking Through the Reverse DCF Math at $318.71
paragraphs: Let us walk through the Reverse DCF inputs and cash-flow reconciliation step by step. At $318.71, enterprise value stands at $1,561.80 billion. Finviz's 33.14x P/FCF implies $49.88 billion in trailing twelve-month free cash flow, compared with audited FY2025 FCF of $31.96 billion and 9M 2026 FCF of NT$1,112.15 billion (~$34.9 billion).

Two adjustments explain that gap. First, 9M 2026 CFO benefited from +NT$169.62 billion (~$5.3 billion) in net customer capacity deposit inflows. Second, ~$40.5 billion in 9M PP&E outlays leaves $19.5 billion to $23.5 billion of implied Q4 capex inside the $60B–$64B annual budget.

Applying a 9.5% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth (16.7x terminal FCF), $1,561.80 billion EV embeds 11.3% annual FCF growth off $49.88 billion, or 17.2% off FY2025's $31.96 billion trough. If AI capex pauses and drops utilization below 75% before capex is cut, FCF compresses toward $25B–$35B (or $35B–$42B only if growth capex is slashed toward $20B maintenance), putting fair EV near $1,100B–$1,300B.

book_subsections.title: Why 13.81x Forward Earnings Still Failed to Hold Support
paragraphs: Investors often assume that a 13.8x forward P/E creates an automatic valuation floor. History disagrees. During the 2022 rate shock and PC/handset inventory bust, TSMC's trailing P/E compressed to 11.2x–11.9x and EV/EBITDA fell to 7.2x–10.1x. Similarly, memory leaders Samsung and Micron looked cheap on single-digit multiples in 2022 right before earnings collapsed under high fixed depreciation.

TSMC's foundry moat is vastly stronger than commodity memory, backed by $93.64 billion in net cash as of September 30, 2026. Even so, when an equity market enters a Downtrend with ten distribution days and a 5.04% Treasury yield, portfolio managers cut high-beta semiconductor exposure regardless of forward P/E.

book_subsections.title: Comparing TSM Against Live Foundry, OSAT, and AI Peers
paragraphs: Across our November 20, 2026 peer snapshot, TSMC remains financially unrivaled while sharing the sector's technical carnage. Mature-node rival UMC trades at 11.45x trailing P/E with a 19.83% ROE and 20.54% operating margin, sitting in Stage 4 at $12.04. Intel posts -10.87% ROE and 10.51% operating margin at $51.28, also stuck in Stage 4. Packaging partner ASE Technology (ASX) earns a 20.53% ROE and 11.46% operating margin at 24.90x P/E, likewise in Stage 4.

Even TSMC's flagship AI customer, NVIDIA ($125.53, 13.49x trailing P/E, 93.33% YoY revenue growth), and analog bellwether Texas Instruments ($263.75, 34.22x P/E) are locked in Stage 4 downtrends. Only Microsoft ($484.52, 25.30x P/E, 34.22% ROE) avoids Stage 4, sitting in Stage 3. That sector-wide breakdown proves TSM's selloff reflects institutional semiconductor de-risking rather than a broken monopoly.

book_subsections.title: Updated 12-Month Valuation Scenarios: Bear $250, Base $425, Bull $550
paragraphs: Because the starting price shifted from $398.73 to $318.71 and macro risk escalated into a formal US Downtrend, we reset our 12-month valuation bands cleanly. In our Bear case, a 2027 AI capex digestion slows forward EPS to $21.50 and compresses the multiple to a 2022-style 11.6x trough, yielding $250.00 (-21.6%). In our Base case, 20%–25% normalized growth and a base recovery re-rate $23.50 forward EPS to 18.1x, yielding $425.00 (+33.4%).

In our Bull case, N2 ramps faster than expected with gross margins above 64%, lifting $25.00 forward EPS to 22.0x and $550.00 (+72.6%), matching the $554.22 Street consensus target. Notice the lesson: TSM offers compelling 12-month fundamental upside from $318.71, yet valuation alone cannot override a broken chart or a triggered stop.

book_subsections.title: Owner Earnings, Footnote Adjustments & Capital Spread
paragraphs: Before placing too much weight on headline P/FCF, recall our Chapter 6 footnote findings. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of NT$2,402.12 billion benefited from customer temporary receipts jumping from NT$189.86 billion to NT$359.48 billion, while NT$167.59 billion in cash government grants offset carrying PP&E and lowered GAAP depreciation. Meanwhile, Q2 net income included a NT$63.20 billion gain from trimming TSMC's VIS stake.

Adjusting for those one-offs still leaves an extraordinary industrial engine generating 32.67% ROIC against a 9.5% cost of capital. That +23.2 percentage point spread ensures TSM will eventually re-rate once the semiconductor tape finishes digesting supply.

book_subsections.title: Separating Maintenance Capex From Growth Capex in Valuation
paragraphs: To understand why TSM looks cheap on forward earnings yet expensive on headline free cash flow, split maintenance capex from growth capex. Keeping seventeen million 12-inch equivalent wafers running takes roughly $18 billion to $22 billion each year. By contrast, TSMC plans $60 billion to $64 billion in FY2026 capital spending, backed by $40.93 billion in November 10 Board approvals.

That means over $40 billion builds fresh N2, A16, and CoWoS cleanrooms rather than replacing worn tools. Stripping out growth spending puts normalized owner earnings above $60 billion a year. Against a $1,561.80 billion enterprise value, you are paying roughly 25x normalized owner cash flow—a reasonable price for a monopoly that simply must prove end-demand stays healthy.
